hot.title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights
hot.summary: The authors show that GPT-6 Astra, a general-purpose frontier LLM, can read and write neural network weights directly, without gradient descent or trained helper models. Across eight experiments it identifies what small networks were trained on from their weights, fixes and writes game-playing policies, and edits 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights to stop reasoning loops. They call this Weight-Space Programming.

hot.title: Hinted Scaling Laws
hot.summary: The authors develop benchmark hinting to forecast downstream accuracy when smaller models score near zero. They add graded solution help, fit its relationship with model scale, and predict the unhinted score. On Delphi, logit mixing predicted 25.9% GSM8K accuracy for a 10^23-FLOP model within 3 percentage points, using models trained with at most 10^20 FLOPs. This result uses a solution-prompted teacher.

hot.title: CoworkOS:Scaling Agent Coworkers for Real-world Automation
hot.summary: CoworkOS addresses complex work by letting a Main Agent direct delegated tasks while a Coordinator tracks assignments and feedback, and Subagents execute bounded work. Persistent jobs, memory, and shared resources support continuity across interruptions. In a five-round post-training case study, the mean across eight benchmark scores rose from 33.19 to 42.95; this measured increase does not isolate CoworkOS’s causal effect.

hot.title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
hot.summary: The authors introduce uni-robot-agent, a shared robot-interaction harness that lets adapters translate common tools and execution feedback across models and environments. On RoboDojo, open-weight Qwen3.8-Flash-Next scores 31.39 without privileged simulator inputs, above the published GPT-6 Astra–RoboProbe score of 28.97; this is not a matched comparison, since evaluations used 252 and 2,100 episodes, respectively.

hot.title: Pixel: A Co-Designed Full-Stack Robot System for Learning General-Purpose Mobile Manipulation
hot.summary: Pixel co-designs a mobile-manipulation robot, demonstration interfaces, controller, and learning system so human and robot demonstrations can use shared task-space actions. A ground-anchored frame expresses head and hand targets together, which a whole-body controller translates into motion. Policies trained on human demonstrations averaged 82.0% task progress, versus 67.3% and 25.7% for alternatives; robot-data joint-space actions scored higher.

hot.title: Automating AI R&D for Molecular Discovery
hot.summary: Intology evaluates Locus, its autonomous AI R&D system, on three molecular discovery tasks: proprietary molecular property prediction, adapting Boltz-2 for small-molecule potency prediction, and designing antibody workflows around BoltzGen/Boltz-2 and ESMC/ESMFold2. Under matched compute, Locus outperforms Claude Code, Codex, and baselines from Boltz and BioHub, generalizing better from limited data and finding more sample-efficient solutions.

hot.title: GSBR: Geometric Support Behavior Regularization for Online RL
hot.summary: GSBR guides online robot learning by penalizing actions only outside neighborhoods around sampled actions from a pretrained controller. This lets the actor choose among supported behaviors while permitting nearby improvements at a distance-based cost. Across 19 tasks in four benchmarks, GSBR averages 95% success and 0.95 normalized throughput, versus RLT’s 0.77; on LIBERO, RLT has higher success.

hot.title: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents
hot.summary: ToolSpace builds executable cross-service task paths from observed tool-call traces, linking adjacent calls through data, state, and retry dependencies. It samples paths whose inputs are available, replays them from initial states, and retains those passing checks. ToolSpace-35B-A3B averages 41.0 across seven benchmarks, versus 23.0 for its backbone and 43.2 after on-policy RL; replay validates chains, not agent success.

hot.title: Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
hot.summary: The authors present targeted guidance, an on-policy self-distillation method for teaching coding agents behaviors missing from their usual attempts. After a failed turn, textual feedback conditions the same model’s token predictions, and distillation applies only to that turn while reinforcement learning rewards remain in the objective. In the semantic-search demonstration, it learned a new format without reducing coding pass rate; generalization beyond this experiment is unestablished.

hot.title: Pretraining Data Scale Reverses the Muon-AdamW Fine-Tuning Gap
hot.summary: The authors compare how AdamW and Muon pretraining affect language-model fine-tuning across five OLMo-style model sizes and four datasets. They measure learning–forgetting frontiers and track the margin-to-spread ratio of next-token logits. Muon leads at lower data budgets, but AdamW often overtakes it beyond task- and model-dependent crossovers, despite Muon’s lower pretraining loss; this does not establish a universal ordering.

hot.title: Pixel-UMI: Learning Environment-Aware Whole-Body Manipulation from Sensorized Human Demonstrations
hot.summary: Pixel-UMI retargets human demonstrations into whole-body robot supervision using reconstructed scene geometry to turn demonstrated head and gripper motion into robot trajectories. EAR balances pose tracking with soft collision avoidance. Camera masking and calibrated labels address viewpoint and timing mismatches. Across three human-demonstration-only tasks, EAR raises average task progress by 64.41 percentage points over retargeting without environment awareness.

hot.title: D&A: Decoupling Description and Assessment Enables VLMs as Zero-Shot Robotic Reward Models
hot.summary: D&A is a prompt-based robot reward method that describes video events before judging them against an explicit task-success criterion. Its vision-language model separates description from assessment, aiming to reduce rewards based on assumed success. On D&A-Bench, Gemini 3 Flash achieves Kendall τₐ of 0.672, versus 0.438 for direct prompting; this shows improved trajectory ranking on that benchmark, not universal performance.

hot.title: EgoActionBench: Benchmarking Dense Action Captioning for Egocentric Human Videos
hot.summary: EgoActionBench evaluates models’ recovery of fine-grained actions, timing, and hand assignments from first-person video. It uses separate left, right, and coordinated-both-hand timelines, scoring semantic content separately from temporal accuracy. The benchmark contains 1,407 episodes and 41,132 human-verified annotations. Task-adapted LLaVA-OV2-8B reaches 47.9 EgoActionScore, versus 24.7 for its unadapted backbone, but remains below human performance; boundaries and motion descriptions remain difficult.

hot.title: Behind Video Generation: Observations and Insights on Multimodal Understanding from Kling
hot.summary: The authors present an understanding stack for video generation that links dense captioning, reference-grounded captioning, prompt enhancement, text encoding, reward modeling, and evaluation. Their Kling captioner scores 21.70 on VidCapBench accuracy, while a smaller variant scores 21.84. In one staged prompt-enhancement setup, StoryEval rises from 65.42 to 76.46; DiT-in-the-loop reinforcement learning improves worst-case quality but can reduce best-case output quality.

hot.title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
hot.summary: DreamX transfers motion from human videos to robot actions without paired human–robot training data. It uses learnable queries to read a pretrained video model’s features and compress motion into a code, which can condition future-video generation or robot action prediction. On LARYBench, it achieves 0.17 average normalized action MSE and 69.67% accuracy; transfer is demonstrated only in evaluated open-loop settings.

hot.title: TAMPAgent: Agentic Belief-Space Planning for Mobile Manipulation
hot.summary: TAMPAgent guides a robot through manipulation by combining an LVLM agent’s hypotheses and plans with a task planner and perception/manipulation tools. The planner translates actions into geometric constraints, and tools certify values for each action before execution. On simulated RBY1 kitchen tasks, absolute success averaged 77.2%, versus 57.2% for CaP and 61.1% for GaP; this does not establish general reliability.

hot.title: IdeaTaste: Do LLMs Share the Research Taste of Human Researchers?
hot.summary: IdeaTaste tests whether AI research agents make choices resembling those of human communities. It generates proposals from literature frozen at the end of 2025, then compares their citations and ideas with papers published in January–August 2026. Agents reach about 26% of human level on citation matching and 18% on idea matching, but publication similarity measures community choices, not objective research quality.

hot.title: Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPAs
hot.summary: The authors test whether positive views can align separately trained text and image representations. A JEPA trained on different descriptions of the same scene learns stronger alignment than one trained on corruptions of a single description. On WIT-1024, the 109M-parameter model scores .184 against DINOv2 ViT-B, exceeding Qwen2.5-72B’s .154; the theorem’s idealized assumptions limit generalization.

hot.title: Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents
hot.summary: Strategist lets a frozen meta-agent search for model-calling strategies, test them, and save reusable blueprints for later tasks. Its models remain unchanged. Across 30 benchmarks, it reports 74.7% mean accuracy versus 74.0% for the strongest baseline and 0.61× weighted inference-token cost. It wins on 24 benchmarks, but does not improve both accuracy and cost universally.

hot.title: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning Improves Long Horizon Agents
hot.summary: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning trains a draft model to propose undesirable framings at selected decisions, prompting the target to write its decision at the start of a fresh verification block. This can change precision in the context without changing the target distribution under exact rejection sampling. On DeepSWE, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 pass rate rose from 60.6% to 67.6%; gains are supported only in tested settings.

Across eight experiments it identifies what small networks were trained on from their weights, fixes and writes game-playing policies, and edits 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights to stop reasoning loops. likes.title: Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm
likes.summary: The authors cast pretraining, midtraining, supervised fine-tuning, and suitable reinforcement-learning updates as maximum-likelihood training with a changing data mixture. In reasoning experiments, unified schedules reach higher accuracy and coverage at larger tested compute budgets, though staged training can lead at intermediate budgets. After coding updates, a 0.76B model with 5% midtraining-data mixing scores 58.47% pass@16 versus 52.12%, limited to this continuation setup.

likes.title: Mistral Large 4
likes.summary: Mistral Large 4 is a multimodal mixture-of-experts model whose authors examine long-context attention for agentic coding. They find architecture variants with similar language-modeling loss can differ on SWE-bench Verified, while knowledge-based evaluations show no analogous gap. The final system restores long-context access in more layers and uses DSA to select past tokens; its benchmark results do not isolate DSA’s effect.

likes.title: Meta$^2$: Precomputing Reusable Knowledge for Online Harness Evolution in Long-Horizon Agents
likes.summary: Meta² teaches an evolver reusable guidance for changing a frozen model’s task harness during a run, rather than selecting one harness for every task. Its Meta-Skill guides when to edit, hold, or avoid changes; edits remain run-local, without held-out verifier feedback. With GPT-5.6-Terra, it reports mean@5 81.00% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and mean@3 44.44% on DeepSWE 1.1, on two tested benchmarks.

likes.title: How to Loop Your Transformer: Loop Scaling, Specialization, and Parallel Inference
likes.summary: The authors study looping, which reuses transformer weights for repeated computation, in dense decoder-only models. They compare loop designs and shifted parallel looping. In tested over-trained conditions, two-loop models at 80 tokens per parameter reach a given DCLM validation bits-per-byte with fewer training FLOPs than vanilla models at 160 tokens per parameter, without establishing general efficiency or latency gains.

likes.title: Training language models in simulation for psychiatric intake
likes.summary: The simulation-trained model improves psychiatric intake conversations by practicing multi-turn encounters with simulated patients and receiving rewards for clinical reasoning, communication, and safety. In a randomized, double-blind crossover study, it received higher psychiatrist transcript ratings than its identically prompted base model in 46 of 60 matched scenario pairs (76.7%). This supports improvement in controlled text encounters, not real-patient safety or effectiveness.

likes.title: Probing Spatial State Representations in Visual Foundation Models
likes.summary: The authors evaluate ten frozen visual representations for whether small probes can read visible scene structure, retain objects after they leave view, predict spatial updates under camera motion, and select goal-directed actions. VideoMAE’s out-of-view bearing error is 36.45°, versus DINOv2’s 65.38°, despite DINOv2’s stronger visible-scene readouts. These offline tests do not establish online memory or reliable robot behavior.

likes.title: Cross-Controller Transfer via In-Context Behavior Adaptation
likes.summary: The authors present a robot policy using examples of commands and resulting motion under a deployment controller, sometimes from another task. This context supplies evidence about controller-dependent expert behavior beyond estimated controller dynamics. On a five-task held-out task–controller evaluation, zero-shot average success was 50.0%, versus 27.0% for system identification; evidence comes from one lab setup and VLA architecture.

likes.title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
likes.summary: ID-WM separates choosing intermediate states from choosing actions to make long-horizon planning in world models manageable. A diffusion model proposes nearby subgoals, and an action-conditioned model searches for actions to reach them, with planning repeated locally. In state-based PushT random-goal trials, it succeeds in 77% versus 21% for single-level world-model MPC; this result is limited to the tested benchmark setting.

likes.title: L3G-World: Real-Time Infinite World Generation with Latent 3D Gaussian Memory
likes.summary: L3G-World generates interactive video worlds using a revisable 3D Gaussian scene memory that stores video-VAE features. It renders this memory into latent conditioning for each video chunk, then updates it by adding missing content and refining visible Gaussians. On DL3DV loop-closure tests, it achieves 16.00 self-consistency PSNR versus 13.96 for Spatia; Matrix-Game 3.0 has lower LPIPS, and tests use static scenes.

likes.title: Robotic Data Inoculation
likes.summary: The authors introduce DI, which keeps a human in control while an online-trained residual policy adds bounded, state-dependent changes to commands; the human can correct these deviations, creating recovery-relevant demonstrations. Across three real-world manipulation tasks, DI has the highest mean in all six task-by-method comparisons. For t-cube offline RL, success is 0.59 ± 0.02 versus 0.42 ± 0.06 with clean teleoperation; the findings do not establish general gains or safety.

likes.title: Rethinking Pre-pretraining
likes.summary: The authors test whether synthetic pre-pretraining (PPT) is a better use of a fixed training-compute budget than natural-language training. They compare synthetic-first and natural-language-only training across scarce-data, plentiful-data, and high-token regimes. Across these tested compute-matched settings, synthetic PPT does not outperform natural-language training on language modeling; this finding is limited to the tested recipes and evaluations.

likes.title: Scale Bounds and Force-Class Obstructions to Physically Realizing OpenAI’s Forced Navier–Stokes Blowup
likes.summary: The authors assess forces supporting OpenAI’s forced-blowup construction and quantify its leading profile’s scale. Assuming the construction meets the stated flow hypotheses, they exclude singularities for specified force classes, including forces whose curl satisfies a unique-continuation condition. For water at molecular core length, the matching radius exceeds 1.63×10¹² Hubble radii; this leading-profile bound does not establish laboratory-time accuracy.

likes.title: Intrinsic Distribution Matching
likes.summary: Intrinsic Distribution Matching (IDM) adds pooled feature-mean and standard-deviation matching to distribution-matching distillation while retaining its score-difference correction and short inference path. In a matched two-evaluation ablation, it raises GenEval from 77.46% to 77.81%. On Z-Image-Turbo 6B, it scores 94.25% on LongText-CN and 90.20% on LongText-EN, highest among compared methods at that budget.

likes.title: Aligning Autoresearch: Co-Improvement between Agents and Humans
likes.summary: The authors study how research agents work with people through benchmark direction, monitoring for reward hacking, multi-turn interaction data, and rubrics for writing. On tested tasks, fine-grained direction lowers Muse Spark’s Rebuttal Bench score from 90 to 43.5; AutoInteract raises Qwen3.5-4B Pass@1 to 43.2, and RL-XAR scores 9.6 versus 8.1. These separate results do not establish safe or general research automation.

likes.title: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers
likes.summary: SpecSlot assigns global communication to low-frequency image carriers while keeping finer output slots local. Each anchor produces multiple slots with disjoint spectral roles, but only one joins dense global attention. On ImageNet-512 it reaches 9.14 FID versus 11.98 for a FLOPs-matched JiT-CM control, with 3.9% fewer conditional forward FLOPs; it remains 0.69 FID worse than JiT-B/16.

likes.title: Gym-Anything for Robotics: Scaling physical simulations with digital agents
likes.summary: Gym-Anything for Robotics uses coding agents to build robotics simulations and tasks, then separate auditors test their evidence and probe for defects. The system selects 120 action groups and builds 25 simulations, forming 200 RoboWorld environments. Claude Opus 5.5 succeeds on 0% of 25 test tasks, while reaching 32% on an easier training subset; these are simulated tasks, not real-robot results.

likes.title: Does Scaling Toward AGI Depend on What System-1 Lets System-2 Execute?
likes.summary: The authors propose conditional interaction as a way to improve scaling efficiency: a low-cost predictor estimates each candidate’s application-specific utility before a costly system executes it. The system admits candidates above a threshold and updates predictions from observed outcomes. Under perfect, free screening and equal execution costs, ideal savings approach 1/ρᵤ, but this is theoretical, not measured.

likes.title: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement
likes.summary: The authors survey agent harnesses as runtime layers that connect video production, interaction with video world models, and system development. They explain how harnesses select context, schedule tools, maintain state, route feedback, and enforce budgets. The framework organizes prior work and evaluation requirements, but no surveyed system shows revised development procedures improve later rounds of video-generator development.
